name: Centro Historico
tagline: The steep old streets around Parque Juarez
description: Xalapa's colonial core built on a slope around Parque Juarez, with the cathedral, the government palace and the narrow Callejon del Diamante running off it. Cafes, cantinas and the market are all here, and the whole of it is walkable if you accept that everything is uphill in one direction.
bestFor: Stays that want the cafes, cantinas and the market within a short walk
pros: The best concentration of cafes, bars and restaurants
Market and all bus routes nearby
Genuine colonial streets with views over the valley
cons: Traffic and noise in the narrow streets
The highest rents in the city, though still low

name: Zona Universitaria and Xalapa 2000
tagline: Around the Universidad Veracruzana, student life and cheap rents
description: The districts holding the university's main faculties, with student housing, cheap fondas, bookshops and the bars that go with a large student population. Rents here are the lowest in the city and the social life is the most accessible for anyone arriving without contacts.
bestFor: Budget stays that want the student scene and the cheapest rooms
pros: Cheap fondas and student bars throughout
University events, cinema and concerts nearby
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes from the historic centre

name: Los Lagos and Paseo de los Lagos
tagline: Around the lakes below the centre, the city's best walk
description: The chain of small lakes and the landscaped path beside them just below the historic centre, with the anthropology museum's approach and quiet residential streets on either side. It is the most attractive part of Xalapa to live in and the walk everyone uses in the mornings.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a green walk out of the door and quiet nights
pros: The lakes path for running and walking
Ten minutes downhill to the centre
cons: Uphill walk back to the centre

name: Animas and the Northern Avenues
tagline: The modern commercial belt, malls and newer apartments
description: The northern part of the city along the avenues out towards the highway, where the malls, supermarkets, chain restaurants and newer apartment complexes have concentrated. It is the least characterful part of Xalapa and the most convenient for anyone who wants a modern flat and parking.
bestFor: Stays wanting a newer apartment, a car and everyday shopping nearby
pros: Newest apartments and the most reliable services
Malls, supermarkets and clinics close by
cons: Twenty minutes from the historic centre

name: Coatepec (12 km south)
tagline: The coffee town in the hills below Xalapa
description: A designated pueblo magico twelve kilometres south, lower and warmer than Xalapa, built around the coffee trade with a colonial centre, coffee mills and the river gorge below. It is prettier and quieter than the city, and the road up takes twenty to twenty-five minutes.
bestFor: Stays that want a small colonial town and the coffee country rather than a city
pros: The coffee mills and the river gorge nearby
cons: Twenty to twenty-five minutes into the city
Limited services and no university life
